title: Nutrition After Weaning: From Milk to the Table
summary: After weaning, your child needs varied nutrition to build their body: protein, vegetables, fruits, and whole grains. Their appetite may fluctuate, and this is normal with the slowing of growth. Offer small, frequent meals, and reduce juices and sweets. Consult a doctor if you notice pallor, lethargy, or clear signs of poor growth.
try_this: This week: Offer your child three small, balanced meals and two healthy light snacks, without forcing quantities.
reflection_prompts: How does your child’s appetite seem these days?

review_defects.why: The Arabic says 'clear poor growth' (directly noticing the growth issue), while the English adds 'signs of', shifting the focus from the condition itself to its indicators.
